bullets: Game 5 of 6 of this single-deck session and the only loss: a Hog cycle mirror-ish matchup against classic 2.6 Hog Cycle (Hog Rider, Evo Cannon, Musketeer, Ice Golem, Ice Spirit, Evo Skeletons, Fireball, The Log). Ryley called it before the start - clock 2:43: 'Whenever I have 2.6, I always beat hog rider earthquake... it's just so hard for us to play, I definitely rather be on the 2.6 end' - and confirmed the result at clock 0:03: 'And uh yeah guys, we lost, man'.

The core loop is Hog Rider at the left bridge tile [1, 15] plus a spell into the middle of the opponent's half to break their defending Cannon, run at clock 2:25, 1:37, 1:09, 0:15 and in overtime at 1:59 and 1:17. Clock 2:19: 'I like to go for those middle earthquakes in this match up... you almost always get a nice hog rider hit out of it if they're not prepared'. (The spell is Earthquake; the pipeline auto-attributed its five deploy labels to the opponent because they land on the enemy half - see the match file's Data gaps.)

Defence is Cannon-centred and reactive: hold the building for the opponent's Hog (clock 1:51, 'I have the cannon ready though just in case he wants to hog rider'), then protect it with Skeletons so it stays on the board (clock 1:14, 'I want the Cannon to live... he has to either spell it away or wait for it to die'), with Firecracker behind it for the Musketeer and Mighty Miner or The Log for whatever tanks.

The self-critique at clock 1:31 is the deck lesson of the match: 'I need to actually build up pushes. I can't just go naked hog rider over and over again or I will just lose this game' - after which he starts every Hog with a back Mighty Miner ([8, 0], [9, 0], [8, 1]) or plays the Hog itself in the back at [1, 2].

He lost the right Princess Tower's health to a lane-switching Hog at clock 0:25-0:23 (4858 -> 3654, 'the hog rider just swerved me'), went to overtime level on towers, and refused to switch his own attack lane at clock 0:35 ('I don't think we want to switch to the same lane. That's the problem') before running out of pressure: 'we're just going to lose cuz we can't apply enough pressure to grab the damage back'.

new_deck.rationale: Average elixir 2.5 with a single fast win condition, 1-elixir cycle cards and a cheap defensive building, replayed every rotation.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: A 2.5-elixir Hog Rider cycle: Hog Rider at the bridge on repeat, a middle spell to break the defending building, and Cannon plus Skeletons, Electro Spirit, Firecracker and The Log to defend for as little elixir as possible. It wins by outcycling the opponent's answer to the Hog and chipping with the spell every rotation; Mighty Miner adds a defensive anti-tank that doubles as a back-placed push starter and a tower-damage ability. In this match Ryley showed both halves of the plan and its main failure mode: the Hog-plus-middle-spell loop is efficient (`> [973s] you almost always get a nice hog rider hit out of it if they're not prepared`), but against 2.6's Evolved Cannon, cycled Musketeers and perfectly timed Logs it stops connecting, and cycling the Hog alone loses (`> [1139s] I can't just go naked hog rider over and over again or I will just lose this game`).
